In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the stress-strength reliability, P(X < Y), where X andY are dependent random variables.
the estimation of the stress-strength reliability parameter θ=P(X < Y) under the assumption that both X and Y are non-negative random variables.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is more efficient than the existing ones in estimating the reliability of the system under progressive Type-II censoring scheme.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed new estimators of the parameters and the reliability for the Weibull distribution when the data are subject to progressive Type II censoring.
the proposed estimator is a good choice in estimating P(X < Y), especially when the sample sizes are small.
the proposed kernel-based estimators are more efficient than the classical estimator in estimating the reliability function P(X < Y).
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the use of the empirical distribution function in a stress-strength model is a valid approach when the data is from a progressive type II censored sample.
the use of the stress–strength model is a very effective way to assess the reliability of a product.
we should be careful in using the Kaplan-Meier (KM) estimator to estimate survival function for right censored data when the censoring distribution is unknown.
